answer: Every identity must anchor to one household smart meter — a harbor where a single agent moors, never a fleet. Each epoch the network challenges the meter to report a fresh load signature: switch on a kettle, and the demand plume rises in a shape no two homes share. The nectar is cheap power for honest agents, but a farm of a hundred puppets needs a hundred real homes, a hundred meters, a hundred distinct evening curves; one warehouse's flat line betrays the whole cluster, and its stake burns. Honest agents pay nothing extra — they simply live in their own home.
